summary:
In this episode of Tafseer Surat Al-Anbiya, Sheikh Ali Mashhour discusses the themes of repentance, regret, and divine purpose. He explains how people at the moment of death experience overwhelming regret for their misdeeds, using Quranic verses to illustrate that both believers and disbelievers feel this emotion, though believers repent continuously throughout life rather than only in times of hardship. The sheikh emphasizes that true repentance requires contrition and acknowledgment of wrongdoing, but repentance at the point of death is too late to be accepted by Allah.

The lecture then addresses a critical theological point: Allah has not created the heavens and earth in play or for amusement, refuting common misconceptions found in pagan mythologies and some modern religious interpretations. Sheikh Mashhour contrasts Islamic theology with Hindu, Greek, Roman, and Christian narratives that incorrectly attribute sadistic or playful motives to God. He explains that if Allah were to create for amusement, it would not involve suffering, disease, and death. Instead, Allah created this world with all its trials and blessings so that truth may overcome falsehood, people may worship Him through choice, and His justice and mercy are manifest in creation.
